We need to implement reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set. Known reduction: given graph G=(V,E) for 3-coloring, construct graph H where each vertex v in V is replaced by three vertices (v,1),(v,2),(v,3) representing color choices, and we add edges to enforce that each original vertex picks at most one color (i.e., make the three vertices a triangle/clique), and also for each original edge (u,v), we add edges between (u,c) and (v,c) for each color c to prevent same color on adjacent vertices. Then independent set of size |V| corresponds to a proper 3-coloring: pick one of the three per vertex, they are independent because we forbid same color adjacency and also vertices of same original vertex are adjacent.

Thus reduction: given instance {"n": n, "edges": [[u,v],...]}, produce instance for IndependentSet with n' = n*3 vertices, edges as described, and k = n.

Edge cases: n=0 => independent set size 0 is yes because k=0. Our reduction would produce n'=0, k=0, which is yes. For n<=3, any graph is 3-colorable => reduction must produce independent set instance that is yes. Since k=n, need independent set of size n. In our construction, a proper coloring exists, so independent set exists. For K4 (n=4, complete graph), not 3-colorable => reduction yields no independent set of size 4.

Implement reduce.py with function reduce(instance). Also need brute-force solvers for both problems and test harness.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The two problems


class ThreeColoring:
    """3-Coloring (graph 3-colorability).

    Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...]}
      * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
        [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

    Yes iff each vertex can be given one of 3 colours so that the two
    endpoints of every edge get different colours. Not every colour has to
    be used.

    Edge cases: n = 0 is yes. Any graph with at most 3 vertices is yes. A
    graph containing 4 mutually adjacent vertices (K4) is no.
    """

    name = '3-Coloring'

    @classmethod
    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        validate_plain_graph(instance)


class IndependentSet:
    """Independent Set.

    Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
      * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
        [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
      * k is any integer.

    Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
    vertices with no edge between any two of them.

    Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
    every set of vertices is independent.
    """
